claims.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
claims.evidence: For fixed labelled bugs B, let A(v) be the bugs hosted in N[v]. Any surveillance system maps each vertex v to a distinct nonempty subset S(v)⊆A(v), which is exactly a matching saturating V in the stated bipartite graph. Conversely, such a matching defines each monitoring zone by M(b)={v:b∈S(v)}⊆N[host(b)], producing a valid system. Enumerating host multisets for every j≤k and testing saturation takes f(k)n^{k+O(1)} time; equivalently, exact-k placements can be used after padding with unused bugs. Testing successive k gives the claimed XP exact procedure.
claims.search_method: Direct two-way reduction from surveillance assignments to saturating bipartite matchings; the matching implementation was also exercised in the exact checker.

claims.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
claims.evidence: If h bugs are hosted in N[X], every code of a vertex in X is a distinct nonempty subset of those h bugs, since a bug hosted outside N[X] cannot hear any x∈X. Hence |X|≤2^h−1 and h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). For component additivity, restricting any global solution to the bugs hosted in a component preserves that component's nonempty distinct codes, giving the lower bound by summation. Conversely, unite optimal component systems after assigning disjoint bug identities; nonempty codes supported on disjoint identity sets cannot agree across components.
claims.search_method: Direct counting argument and both directions of the component decomposition.

claims.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Applying the regional bound to X=C forces at least ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs in C. If u is universal in C, placing exactly that many bugs at u makes every nonempty subset available to every vertex; there are at least |C| such subsets, so distinct codes can be assigned. Component additivity yields the sum. Connected components and a vertex of degree |C|−1 can be found in polynomial time.
claims.witness: For each component C, place ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs at a universal vertex and assign its vertices any |C| distinct nonempty subsets of those bugs.
claims.search_method: Matching lower and constructive upper bounds, followed by component decomposition.

claims.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
claims.evidence: Double-counting vertex-bug incidences gives sum_v |S(v)|=sum_b |M(b)|. Each M(b) is contained in the closed neighborhood of its host and therefore has size at most rho, so the sum is at most k rho. Since the S(v) are n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set, their total size is at least L(n,k). The stated inequality follows. Taking subsets by increasing cardinality proves the draft's displayed closed form for L.
claims.search_method: Direct incidence double count; exact enumeration independently checked the L formula and L(n,k)≥2n−k for all 120 cases with 1≤k≤6.

claims.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
claims.evidence: A connected graph of maximum degree two is a path or cycle. In an interval representation, an induced cycle of length at least four is impossible: choose a cycle interval with minimum right endpoint; both cycle neighbors contain that endpoint and hence intersect, forming a chord. Thus the connected possibilities are P_n and K3. For P_n, the incidence bound with rho≤3 and L(n,k)≥2n−k gives k≥ceil(n/2). For even n=2t≥4, equality k=t would force every bug to monitor a full three-vertex neighborhood, all t singleton codes to occur, and every remaining code to have size two. Consequently hosts must be distinct, internal, and pairwise nonadjacent: cohosted bugs could not have singleton codes, while bugs at adjacent hosts would give both host vertices the same two-bug code. But P_{2t} has only t−1 pairwise nonadjacent internal vertices. Hence k≥t+1; P2 is separately ruled out with one bug by the code count. Bugs on odd vertices attain the odd-path bound; for an even path, adding a bug at the last vertex attains t+1. K3 has optimum two. Component additivity completes the result.
claims.witness: On P_n, host bugs at vertices 1,3,5,... and, when n is even, additionally at vertex n; use singleton codes at hosts and adjacent-host pairs at intervening vertices. On K3, two bugs at a universal vertex realize its three nonempty codes.
claims.search_method: Structural interval-graph classification, incidence lower bound, equality-case analysis, and constructive upper bound; exhaustive matching checked P_n for 1≤n≤12 and K3.

claims.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
claims.evidence: Exact endpoint ordering is L1,L2,L3,L4,L5,L6,U,R6,R4,R5,R3,R1,R2. Literal recomputation of the source's lexicographic feasibility test produces placements (processing,host)=((1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13)); reflecting the entire instance produces the same seven-placement trace. Exact overlap checks confirm reflection symmetry and connectivity. The displayed six-bug codes are all legal, nonempty, and pairwise distinct. For X_L={L1,L2,L3,L4}, N[X_L]={L1,...,L6}; the reflected four-vertex set has closed-neighborhood union {R1,...,R6}. These unions are disjoint, and each set of four vertices requires three hosted bugs, proving OPT≥6. Thus OPT=6. As an independent finite check, all 6,188 five-bug host multisets were rejected by exact saturating matching.
claims.search_method: Exact Fraction-based interval ordering and greedy simulation in both orientations, certificate validation, regional lower bounds, and exhaustive matching over every five-bug host multiset.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a polynomial-time approximation with ratio strictly below 2 for arbitrary interval instances or an appropriate matching inapproximability theorem. The draft establishes neither: its XP algorithm is not polynomial for unrestricted k, its exact formula concerns only restricted components, its bounds do not imply approximation hardness, and the greedy witness shows only a 7/6 nonexactness example. These are correct and material structural/algorithmic advances, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate rather than FULLY_RESOLVES_TARGET. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and its final writeup explicitly states that the general threshold remains unresolved, making the claimed resolution ACCURATE and not overclaimed.
